newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends down after new four-month low.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends down after new four-month low.

text.p: Cocoa futures hit a new four-month low on Tuesday but trade buying on the dips helped the contracts to finish just above the session floor.
Traders said fresh selling and further fund long liquidation continued to take a toll on prices. But in contrast to Monday's sell-off, today's losses were relatively small amid narrow trade.
After two straight days of losses, traders said market prospects remained poor. "It looks a bit weak," said one floor source.
Benchmark September flipped below 970 stg to touch a low at 968, a new four-month low, before recovering slightly to end 10 off at 975.
"It found some good buying support at 970," said one trader.
Manufacturers were also seen buying. But origins were sidelined.
Analysts had hoped that September would close above 980 stg to allow it to stay above a key uptrend.
Cocoa could now be trading at a new, lower range between 960 and 980 stg, said one. After the initial support at 960, the next key level is the mid-February trough of 895 stg.
There was no fundamental news behind the move, which has sliced values by 4.6 percent in two days.
On Monday, speculators relentlessly unloaded their long positions after the market posted a key chart reversal.

The heavy liquidation was reflected in Tuesday's data which showed a fall of 3,583 lots in uncovered September positions to 17,968 as at the close of business on Monday. But the March position showed a rise of 1,225 to 35,013.
"Many people were getting out of the market," the trader said.
Sept/Dec switches were traded at 35-37 stg and Dec/March at 24-25.
On the fundamental front, broker GNI said it believed that a crop in excess of 1.2 million tonnes is possible for Ivory Coast next year if favourable conditions remain through November.
